_: Pinned occurrences of internal vocabulary in this PUBLIC repo. Codes are defined by scripts/guard-public-vocabulary.py --legend; they are codes rather than words so that this file needs no self-exclusion from the scan. Every entry carries a measured count and a reason; an entry without a real reason is a defect.

V1.why: public API of this SwiftPM package. V1 names a public enum, three public static functions and two error cases that customers compile against, plus the doc comments that explain them. Renaming them is a SOURCE-BREAKING change to a published package, so it is an owner decision, not a text edit.

V11.why: public refusal and verdict CONTRACT, not prose. These are the wire strings a caller switches on: two V1_* error codes, one V2_ATTACH_REFUSED code, and the six hyphenated verdicts the evaluator returns (each spells a V-code by construction). Changing any of them changes behaviour for every integrator: owner-level.

V13.why: a DATED changelog entry (history, 2026-07) that recorded the enterprise-only tier under its legacy name as cloud-only at the time. Owner ruling 2026-09-11: enterprise-only, ad hoc, no public surface names it -- every forward-looking line is gone (protocol, registry, Dart mirror, examples, design doc); a changelog is a contemporaneous record and rewriting it falsifies the record, so this ONE historical mention stays pinned at 1.

V9.why: the platform door's query PARAMETER NAME, not prose: the Android Essence 2 store's member door is `/v1/agent/<code>/model/download?model=essence-2&member=android_store.v1.json&<V9>=android`, the URL essence2-android's MeteredDoorResolver fetches from, and the entitlement window must ask exactly that door (PR #202 round 3). Renaming it is a platform API change (public-api-service), not a text edit. One occurrence: EntitlementWindow.storeDoor's URL.

V10.why: ordinary English in sample and plugin code: the graphics sense of V10 (putting a crop back onto a frame), an audio-graph loop and buffer named with it, and a third party's own use of the -ing form in a quoted protocol note. V10 deliberately matches the -ite and -ing forms, so it over-matches here. Pinned rather than narrowed: a narrowing wide enough to clear these would also blind the real blend-stage use.
